EXISTENCE: no source found anywhere names 'Dadu-Sui Gas Pipeline' by that exact title except gem.wiki itself (inaccessible, and banned as a citation regardless) and AI-search syntheses that are visibly just echoing the gem.wiki page content back (one such synthesis asserted an unsourced 'contracted for reverse flow to SNGPL' / 'Indus Right Bank Pipeline System' label -- that label appears on no independently-reachable page I could load, so I am treating it as a search-engine hallucination artifact and NOT using or citing it). However, the underlying physical claim -- a gas transmission corridor running from the Sui field in Balochistan through Sindh, with Dadu as a real intermediate hub on that corridor -- IS independently corroborated: (1) Wikipedia's Sui Southern Gas Company article states the SSGC transmission system 'extends from Sui, Balochistan to Karachi, Sindh' and documents the original 1955 mainline (347 mi / 16 in / 110 MMcf/d) built on this exact route; (2) Dawn (an independent Pakistani daily, unrelated to GEM or gem.wiki) ran a news item specifically about a gas-supply disruption 'from Dadu field' affecting both SSGC and SNGPL, confirming Dadu is a genuine, currently-active node in this same transmission grid, not an invented place; (3) an aggregate industry-data page (offshore-technology.com) independently confirms SSGC operates an extensive Balochistan-to-Sindh transmission network (spanning up to 24 in diameter pipe), consistent with a network large enough to contain a discrete ~266 km / 20 in Sui-to-Dadu segment. None of these three name 'Dadu-Sui' as a specific segment or corroborate its exact length/diameter/capacity -- that gap is flagged separately below -- but together they rule out 'GEM-only entity / hallucination' as the concern here: this reads as a real segment of a well-documented, decades-old physical corridor, just one whose segment-level specs I could not independently pin down this run. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' fits -- this is a long interprovincial trunk segment of the historic Sui-Karachi mainline, not a field-gathering or plant-feed line. DUPLICATE CHECK against the full 63-row roster: not a duplicate of P4019 Dadu-Malir-Karachi Gas Pipeline (same Dadu endpoint, but P4019 runs the OTHER direction, Dadu onward to Malir/Karachi -- the two rows read as complementary upstream/downstream segments split at the same Dadu junction, not an overlapping double-count: combined length 266+250=516 km lines up reasonably with the original ~558 km/347-mile Sui-Karachi mainline Wikipedia describes, before any later loop lines); not a duplicate of P4024 Hassan-Sui or P4075 Pir Koh-Sui (both are short field-gathering laterals feeding INTO Sui from nearby Balochistan fields, entirely different geography and function from a Sui-to-Dadu trunk leg). ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100% is geographically consistent -- both Sindh (Dadu) and Balochistan (Sui) sit within SSGC's documented service/transmission territory, distinct from SNGPL's Punjab/KPK territory -- so nothing here looks wrong, though (as with the specs) no source names SSGC as owner of this segment specifically, only of the network generally.
